target_customer: Enterprises whose teams use different chat platforms such as Slack, Teams, Webex, Zoom and Google Chat
problem: Workplace chat apps are walled gardens, so colleagues and partners on different platforms cannot message each other natively.
business_model: B2B SaaS and partner channel subscriptions for chat interoperability

founders.name: Tom Hadfield
previous_startups: Soccernet.com (sold to ESPN for 40 million dollars, per YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page says he sat on the board of Heifer International.

founders.name: James Cundle
founders.background_notes: YC page describes a repeat technical co-founder with security and DevOps experience.

technical_complexity.rationale: Relaying and translating messages between platforms with different APIs and permissions needs ongoing integration work with each vendor, and later native-looking delivery is harder.

defensibility.rationale: Depends on platform APIs and partnerships; a platform owner could build bridging itself, and no moat was measured in sources.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Rather than copying it, Zoom and Cisco invested in the Series A in December 2021 and committed to interoperability APIs; Google also partnered.

market_need_then: In November 2016 SiliconANGLE covered Message.io as a translator for chatbots across Slack and HipChat, showing early bot ecosystem fragmentation. Enterprise demand for cross-platform chat grew later, as the Series A story notes.

branding.domain_note: Moved from message.io to the short m.io domain; dates not sourced.

rebrands.why: Not stated by any source opened. One CB Insights profile also lists an earlier name Prompt App.

brand_strength.rationale: Short name and domain help, but no source shows community, memes or brand press, and Mio is confused with Mio.xyz and unrelated Mio products.

pivots.from: Bot syndication for chatbots across Slack, HipChat and Skype
pivots.to: Chat interoperability between workplace messaging platforms, later Google Workspace and Microsoft 365
pivots.why: Not stated; sequence inferred from SiliconANGLE 2016 and the company site now. Exact date unknown.

outcome_analysis: Mio started as Message.io, a bot syndication seed company in 2016 with Khosla and Eniac, raised a small 2018 round, then landed Zoom and Cisco as strategic investors in the December 2021 Series A. It now positions as Google's official interoperability partner and lists enterprise customers like Walmart and Sony. Total raised is disputed across sources, so scale is uncertain.
notes: Seed date inferred as 2016 from search summaries; the Built In article date was not seen. Total raised is reported as about 17 million (TechCrunch coverage summary), 12 million, or 29.12 million (CB Insights), conflicting; treat totals as unverified. Founding year conflicts: November 2015 (YC page, Wikipedia) versus 2016. The 2018 round was reported as 5.75 million by Built In only. No competitor with a source dated near the batch was found; the SiliconANGLE article does not name rivals.
